newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Daiwa raises its forecasts for Hungary shr market.
newsitem.headline: Daiwa raises its forecasts for Hungary shr market.

text.p: Daiwa Europe Ltd said it raised its earnings forecasts for Hungarian shares for 1997 and also raised its year-end target for the BUX index.

"After boosting our earnings projections for this year, we have also raised our year-end target for the BUX index from 6,500 to 7,000," Chief equity strategist Roger Monson said in the June issue of its "Equity Strategy Quarterly."
"(This) would bring the market to a price per earnings ratio of 14.9 times for 1997, but a more relevant 11.6 times for 1998," he said.
On Thursday the BUX index finished at 6,450.68 points, having risen more than 50 percent since the beginning of 1997.

Monson said that along with an improving economy, Hungarian stocks were supported by an excellent earnings record, with the 11 leading companies reporting net income up 46 percent in the first quarter.

This pace may slow somewhat by the end of the year, but Monson said that "as a result of the Q1 outturn and the comments made by managements on the full year, we have boosted our 1997 market earnings per share growth projection by five points to 34 percent".
In terms of risk profile Hungary could stand a comparison with several western European countries and outperform most of central and eastern Europe (CEE), Monson said.
"Hungary's overall risk profile for equity investors would now compare favourably with many western European countries, and is clearly ahead of most CEE peers," he said.
